summary: Successor gate at repair head 2ea7f584f0ca91a9de470ebe72b4063e8685de02 (fork branch solr-17764-submit, re-verified live at filing; prior gate's stop and canonical release were reconciled before execution under pr-5315-gate-stop-reconciliation-20261111). PASSED: the stage-A focused run (async diagnostic test and the new mixed-route test, seed 17764C0DE); the server lockfile truth check (Gradle regeneration in a disposable checkout is byte-for-byte identical to the pushed hand edit and changed no file anywhere); the corrected fail-before mutation (removing only the outer whole-batch guard makes testMixedRouteFailureDoesNotReplayMarkedRejection fail with 'Expected exception RouteException but no exception was thrown', against its pass at head); the full suites CloudSolrClientCacheTest 13/13, CloudHttp2SolrClientRetryTest 1/1, CloudSolrClientRoutingTest 2/2, ProbeGracefulRejectionJettyBodyCloseTest 1/1, ProbeGracefulMultiShardTest 1/1 and TestGracefulJettyShutdown 1/1 with nightly enabled; installDist builds the distribution; tidy is clean. The six pre-existing 503 regression methods in CloudSolrClientCacheTest are unchanged by the repair diff (its only change is the added mixed test), so the r4 gate's fail-before evidence for them stands in the lineage. Three findings make the verdict failed; each is itemized in findings, including the packaged-server leg, which was run three times with the attempt history disclosed.

findings.detail: In the full ProbeGracefulRejectionClientTest run the class is 13/14: testAsyncMarkedUpdateIsNotReplayedByEitherTransport fails, as it did at the previous head, while the same method passes when run in isolation (stage A of this gate). The diagnostic build captured the full chain and the endpoint counts the gate record required: jetty=true transport, rejected requests=1, healthy requests=0, so NO application update was resent; the replay charge is acquitted. What surfaces instead is java.util.concurrent.ExecutionException wrapping org.apache.solr.client.solrj.SolrServerException, thrown from HttpJettySolrClient's onFailure (line 443) via processErrorsAndResponse (line 619), caused by java.nio.channels.AsynchronousCloseException at InputStreamResponseListener.close: on the Jetty async path, when the error response stream closes, the failure is delivered as a generic server exception rather than the marked-rejection type the feature's contract promises, and which exception a caller sees is timing-dependent (passes isolated, fails in company). Per the gate record the named test must pass at the exact head for a passed verdict; it does not reliably do so, and the underlying cause is a real client defect, narrower than replay but squarely in the feature's contract.

Root check -x test fails at :solr:core:validateSourcePatterns: ProbeGracefulMultiShardTest.java line 57 declares its logger as LoggerFactory.getLogger(ProbeGracefulMultiShardTest.class), the class-literal form the source-pattern rules reject (invalid logger name; not the MethodHandles idiom). The file is the branch's own core test and the line predates the repair head; the previous gate never reached this task because the server lockfile failure fired first. No other check failure was observed. One-line repair for the implementation worker.

installDist succeeds and the distribution ships the wiring (server/modules/graceful.mod with etc/jetty-graceful.xml; bin/solr starts the server with --module=graceful). Three stop attempts were made against the packaged server on port 18983 with the vendored JDK 21. Attempt 1 was under-instrumented and is not counted. Attempt 2 produced a script-side false positive (a grep counting defect in the gate harness declared a capture on an ordinary 200 response with no marker); it is discarded in full and disclosed here so it is never cited. Attempt 3, fully instrumented: six client connections were mid-upload (100-continue received, bodies trickling at a limited rate) when bin/solr stop began; all six were aborted within about a second, 600-per-second-class probes recorded zero 503 responses of any kind and no marker header, and the socket closed. The packaged stop path as driven by bin/solr stop therefore exhibits no graceful rejection phase in this environment: in-flight work is cut and new requests are refused at the socket, not answered with a marked 503. Whether the stop-monitor path bypasses the graceful handler or the handler needs a different trigger is a design question for the implementation worker; what this gate establishes is that the deployment behavior the feature exists to produce was not demonstrated, and the observed behavior contradicts it. (The Solr 11 CLI on this distribution has no create_core command and the ad hoc core creation used in the attempts did not take effect; the uploads therefore targeted a nonexistent core path. The uploads were nevertheless accepted connections with bodies in flight at the Jetty layer when stop began, which is the layer the marker handler occupies; the classification does not depend on core existence, but the caveat is recorded.)

trust_note: Unchanged from the prior gate: accepting a forged marker when trust is explicitly enabled is an operator-trust precondition of the design, not provenance verification. The candidate does not address ambiguous in-flight update 503s.
